chunks: From him, and from someone else, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said to a man: 'Be content with what Allah has distributed to you, and do not look at what is with others, and do not covet what you cannot attain, for whoever is content is satisfied, and whoever is not content is not satisfied is not satisfied, and take your share from the Hereafter.'

And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The most beneficial thing for a person is his precedence over people in finding fault with himself, and the most difficult thing in terms of cost is hiding poverty, and the least beneficial thing is giving advice to one who does not accept it and being in the neighborhood of the greedy, and the most comforting of comforts is despairing from people.'

And he said: 'Do not be irritable or ill-mannered, and humble yourself by bearing those who oppose you, those who are above you, and those who have preference over you, for you only acknowledge their preference so that you do not oppose them, and whoever does not acknowledge the preference of anyone is self-conceited.'

And he said to a man: 'Know that there is no honor for one who does not humble himself to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and no elevation for one who does not become humble before Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

And he said to a man: 'Organize the affairs of your religion as the people of the world organize the affairs of their world, for the world has been made as a witness by which the hidden matters of the Hereafter are recognized, so recognize the Hereafter by it, and do not look at the world except with consideration.'
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical teachings of Imam al-Sadiq regarding contentment and the relationship between the world and the Hereafter?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises contentment with divine decree, self-reflection over criticizing others, and humility to attain honor. He emphasizes that the worldly life serves as a witness and indicator for the Hereafter, urging believers to manage their religious affairs with the same diligence people manage their worldly affairs.
